issues.detail: The Greek 'εκ της δεξιας του' means 'from the right [hand] of him'. The Vietnamese 'từ tay hữu của' (from the right hand of) is a common interpretation, but strictly speaking, the Greek does not specify 'hand' (cheir). However, more importantly, the Vietnamese 'tay hữu' is a literal translation of 'right hand', whereas the Greek implies 'the right side'. Given the context of the throne, 'right side' is the accurate spatial location.
